system.name: ADR
system.one_liner: an adaptive fail-slow detection library that tracks value and update-frequency history to flag slow faults

content.subject: how ADR updates value/frequency state from a traced variable and decides slow, fatal, or reset

content.key_idea: ADR raises value/frequency history into two state checkers, using a frequency-increase signal to reset windows and a sustained value slowdown to declare a fatal fail-slow event.
content.reading_order: Top-left code snippet produces X_new, flowing right into ① Update value and down into ② Update frequency, both feeding ③ Check fatal.

evidence: ADR monitors both the value and the update frequency of some tracing variables defined in the system code
It employs two state checkers to make decisions, which either trigger internal actions (reset windows)
if they show a sustained slowdown, ADR identifies a slow fault and triggers a fatal action

summary: Figure 9 gives an overview of ADR, the fail-slow detection library, as three colour-coded numbered stages. A WAL.java code snippet shows the traced variable X being sampled into X_new at each execution. Stage (1) Update value pushes X_new onto a value history, checks it against a fixed threshold T or, once the saturated history allows it, against its own p99, producing a red 'Slow' signal and an updated value state. Stage (2) Update frequency records the time gap since the last update into a frequency history and classifies it against upper/lower bounds. Stage (3) Check fatal chains a Frequency state checker (higher resets the sliding windows as a workload change; lower proceeds) into a Value state checker (slower yields a red 'Fatal' action, normal yields Reset).
summary_zh: 图9为ADR总览：代码采样出X_new，①更新数值（比较阈值T或p99，得到Slow），②更新频率（比较时间间隔与上下界），③检查致命——频率变高则重置窗口，变低则看数值状态，持续变慢判Fatal，否则重置。
